extracted_information: The provided web content details the structure of Project Zomboid mod folders, focusing on local installations and Steam Workshop development. It outlines the differences between Build 41 and Build 42 mod structures, the purpose of common and versioning folders, the contents of the `media` folder, and mentions key files like `mod.info` and `workshop.txt`. The primary locations for mods are `Zomboid/mods/` (manual installs) and `Zomboid/workshop/` (development/Steam Workshop).

temporal_info.build_41: Mod structure used in Project Zomboid Build 41.
temporal_info.build_42: Mod structure introduced in Project Zomboid Build 42, adding common and versioning folders. This build's structure is considered for the detailed explanations.
temporal_info.last_updated: This page was last edited on 24 May 2025, at 21:24.

root_folders.description: Location for manually installed mods, not recommended for mod development, located in the cache folder.
Folder used for mod development and uploading to the Steam Workshop, highly suggested for development, located in the cache folder.

workshop_folder_structure.description: Example structure for a single mod project intended for workshop upload.

contents.name: Contents/
contents.description: Folder containing the actual mod content to be uploaded.

subfolders.name: mods/
subfolders.description: Contains the actual mod(s). Each mod here needs a mod.info file to be recognized. This folder is uploaded to the Workshop.

contents.name: workshop.txt
contents.description: File containing information needed to upload the mod to the Steam Workshop. See workshop.txt page for details.

contents.name: preview.png
contents.description: Image used as the mod preview on Steam Workshop. Game imposes a 256x256 resolution.

mod_folder_structure_build_41.description: Structure for a mod within the Contents/mods/ folder in Build 41.

contents.name: mod.info
contents.description: Core file of the mod, required for the mod to be recognized.

mod_folder_structure_build_42.description: Structure for a mod within the Contents/mods/ folder in Build 42, includes versioning and common folders.

contents.name: common/
contents.description: Mandatory folder for Build 42 mods, even if empty. Used to store large files (models, textures, animations) shared across versions.

contents.name: buildVersion(.majorUpdate)(.minorUpdate)/
contents.description: Versioning folders (e.g., 42, 42.1, 42.1.5). Useful for supporting older game versions. Should contain code files and mod.info as they often change with game versions. Loaded after the common folder, overwriting common files if present.

contents.name: mod.info
contents.description: Core file of the mod, required for the mod to be recognized. Typically located within versioning folders in Build 42.

contents.name: poster.png
contents.description: Poster image for the mod. Typically located within versioning folders in Build 42.

contents.name: icon.png
contents.description: Icon image for the mod. Typically located within versioning folders in Build 42.

common_and_versioning_folders.description: Introduced in Build 42 to manage different mod versions per game version.
loading_order: Closest versioning folder to the game version (overwrites common files)
notes: Common folder is not recognized by Build 41 modding structure.
Common folder is mandatory for your mod to work in Build 42, even if empty.

media_folder.description: Contains mod assets. Subfolders are usually the same as the game's media folder.

common_subfolders.name: lua
common_subfolders.description: To program with Lua using the API.

common_subfolders.name: scripts
common_subfolders.description: To create scripts for items, sounds, models, vehicles, crafts, etc.

common_subfolders.name: AnimSets
common_subfolders.description: XML files which are used to define how animations are triggered.

common_subfolders.name: clothing
common_subfolders.description: XML files which are used to define clothing items and outfits.

common_subfolders.name: textures
common_subfolders.description: For texture files used on models.

common_subfolders.name: ui
common_subfolders.description: For images used in UI elements.

notes: Files in the parent folder of the media folder can technically be read from the Lua API within the media folder.

mod_info_file.description: Core file of a mod. Required for the game to recognize the mod. Details are found on a separate page (linked).

script_files.description: Files used to define game elements like items, sounds, vehicles, crafts, etc. Located within the 'scripts' subfolder of the 'media' folder.

lua_files.description: Files containing Lua code used for mod logic and programming. Located within the 'lua' subfolder of the 'media' folder. Can be structured into 'client/', 'server/', and 'shared/' subfolders.
